challenges.instruction: Learn how `oo` adds a small detail to dinner and family phrases, then answer mixed prompts one at a time.

rows.label: family
rows.prompt: the family sitting at the table

rows.label: guest
rows.prompt: a guest who is in the house

lessonSlides.title: `oo` adds a useful detail
lessonSlides.description: Use `oo` to attach one extra idea to a noun phrase. Keep the phrase short.
focusPoints: `qoyska oo miiska fadhiya` adds what the family is doing
`bariis oo diyaar ah` adds the state of the food

rows.label: family
rows.prompt: the family sitting at the table

practiceRows.label: family
practiceRows.prompt: the family sitting at the dinner table
practiceRows.rule: Use `oo` to add the dinner-table action. Do not repeat the plain study example.

practiceRows.label: food
practiceRows.prompt: meat that is ready for dinner
practiceRows.rule: Use `oo` to add a dinner-related state. Do not repeat the plain study example.
answers: hilib oo casho u diyaar ah

practiceRows.label: drink
practiceRows.rule: Use `oo` with the tea phrase from the dinner lesson. Do not repeat the plain study example.

practiceRows.label: guest
practiceRows.prompt: a guest sitting at the dinner table
practiceRows.rule: Use `oo` to connect the guest and the dinner-table action. Do not repeat the plain study example.
